principle: The product does not prescribe what a repository should become; it identifies and strengthens the foundations that allow each repository to succeed at what it is intended to be.
refinementRule: Domains and kinds are data, not a taxonomy. Add, split, merge or re-weight one here; every change stays covered by the foundation-domains.json integrity gate and the module-smoke fixture set. Never add a domain the product cannot evidence from visible repository state, and never let a conclusion cite the absence of findings as evidence.

conclusions.strengthen: A domain is missing, weak or unclear, and a preview-first next action is offered.
conclusions.appropriate-as-is: Every applicable domain is present, or the repository is archived, intentionally minimal or externally managed - and the evidence says why.
conclusions.insufficiently-understood: The product cannot reach a conclusion and names what it would need. A finding about the product, not the repository.

domains.title: Documentation
domains.question: Can a newcomer understand and use this repository from what is written down?

domains.title: Purpose
domains.question: Is it clear what this repository is for and who it serves?
domains.note: The README contract's Overview/Usage section check is skipped under the doc-standards v1 schema, so purpose reads from readmeScore until the section check surfaces as its own signal.

nextAction.label: Preview a README that states the purpose

domains.title: Planning
domains.question: Is there a credible plan or roadmap for what comes next?

domains.title: Structure
domains.question: Is the layout maintainable and navigable by intent?

domains.title: Intentional engineering
domains.question: Is there evidence the work is deliberate - tests, CI, releases, conventions?

evidenceModel.decision: Defined, not scored. Release 3.7's ten repositories decide which evidence earns a detector; until then the domain reports what it observes without judging it.

subAreas.evidence: A test tree or test-runner configuration exists.
A CI workflow or pipeline definition exists.
The latest Actions run concluded successfully; pull requests are not piling up unreviewed.
Recent commits; a clean tree; work on the default branch or a named branch.
Conventions written down (CONTRIBUTING, lint and format configuration) and a layering the tree makes visible.
Tags or releases and a changelog that names them.

kinds.title: Not yet classified
kinds.note: No kind signal; every scored domain applies. A curation or classifier signal refines this.

applicability.planning: A minimal utility with no pending work needs no roadmap.

kinds.title: Externally managed

applicability.planning: Plans live with the upstream owner.

kinds.reason: Externally managed: the upstream owner decides its plan and layout.

kinds.title: Archived

applicability.planning: An archived repository plans no further work.
applicability.structure: An archived repository is not reorganized.
applicability.intentional-engineering: An archived repository is not judged on ongoing engineering.

kinds.reason: Archived: intentionally closed, kept for reference.

kindDetection.note: Only signals the index already carries. Anything undetected is 'unknown' - honest, and every scored domain applies.
